### 1 — Scene
A leafy green salad topped with what appears to be cooked salmon and a few bread pieces. The protein and bread identification is somewhat uncertain because of the lighting.

### 2 — Vessel
A shallow dinner plate, approximately **26 cm** in diameter.  
Vessel area = 3.14 × 13² = **531 cm²**.

### 3 — Items
- Mixed leafy greens, predominantly spinach
- Cooked salmon pieces, apparently with some skin
- Small bread pieces near the upper edge
- No clearly distinguishable dressing or oil, so none is added separately

### 4–7 — Area, volume, weight, and energy
The area shares below divide the visible food footprint without double-counting overlapping ingredients.

| Item | Plate area | Area × height = gross volume | Bulk density | Estimated weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Leafy greens | 55% | 292 cm² × 2 cm = 584 ml | 0.15 g/ml | 88 g | 23 | 20 kcal |
| Cooked salmon | 20% | 106 cm² × 1.3 cm = 138 ml | 0.95 g/ml | 131 g | 206 | 270 kcal |
| Bread pieces | 8% | 42 cm² × 1.4 cm = 59 ml | 0.30 g/ml | 18 g | 265 | 48 kcal |

**Coverage check:** 55% + 20% + 8% = **83%**, consistent with a mostly covered plate and an exposed rim.

### 8 — Sanity check
The estimate is **237 g and 338 kcal**. This is plausible for a mostly covered but relatively light salad: the leaves occupy much of the visible volume, while the salmon supplies most of the weight and energy. Any dressing not distinguishable in the photo is excluded.
